validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independent of GEM. The sheet's own ref (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines) is a navigation page that never names this project (existing_ref_checks on 5 of the 6 HAS_REF units say so; the other 3 say the value string is simply absent) -- so I went to the underlying dated EIA workbooks instead of the nav URL. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook has carried a discrete row for 'Gillis Access Project Extension | TC Energy' in every release from 2023-04 (first appearance, status Announced) through 2026-08 (still tracked, status Approved), a project first-appearance-to-present arc that is independent government tracking, not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is consistent with the project's own description in every EIA release -- a large-diameter (39 mi), high-capacity (1,400 MMcf/d) header/connector line built to move Haynesville production to Louisiana LNG and industrial markets, not a gathering or distribution line; TC Energy's own site describes the parent Gillis system the same way ('a header system that can be further expanded... to serve downstream LNG, industrial and other markets'). No reclassification needed. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 44-row roster -- no other row shares this project's termini/spec combination; the roster note correctly places the Gillis Access MAIN LINE under a different PID (P5416, batch A2) -- see cross_row_leads. ATTRIBUTION: Operator/Owner1=TC Energy 100% is confirmed by EIA's pipeline_operator_name field in all 14 releases AND independently by TC Energy's own corporate site, which identifies 'TC Louisiana Intrastate Pipeline LLC (TCLI)' as the entity behind the Gillis-hub buildout the Extension extends. SPEC: Length 39 mi, Capacity 1,400 MMcf/d, StartYear1 2027, and Status=proposed(=EIA Approved) all agree with EIA's Aug2026 (and prior) release -- see fills. CAVEAT #1 (single-origin risk): every numeric confirmation above traces to one origin (EIA); I searched FERC eLibrary (a JS/Angular SPA that returns only an app shell to curl/WebFetch -- could not query dockets CP26-33 / CP25-521 that EIA's 2026-01+ releases now carry), Federal Register full-text search (no notice matched 'Gillis Access' + TC Energy), NGI and oilgasleads.com (both surfaced only the ORIGINAL 2022-sanctioned $400M/1.5-Bcf/d/2024-in-service Gillis Access mainline, not this Extension -- routed to P5416 instead), TC Energy's own Louisiana Intrastate Pipeline page (also describes only the completed 42-mi/1.5-Bcf/d mainline, not the Extension by name), and oilandgaswatch.org (its pipeline pages are a JS SPA that 403s its own API without a session token; unreachable anonymously). No second independent source that actually names 'Gillis Access Project Extension' and states its numbers was found -- fills below are staged at tier=medium, not high, for that reason. CAVEAT #2 (name-collision hazard, flagging for future researchers): a Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline 'Gillis Header Project' (FERC docket CP26-52-000, filed 2025-12-19) ALSO involves header facilities at 'the existing Gillis Compressor Station' in Beauregard Parish -- a completely different company/project sharing the 'Gillis' name. An early web-search synthesis I ran conflated the two (attributing Cheniere's 36-inch header/Solar Titan turbine/Beauregard-Calcasieu details to this TC Energy row); I verified the conflation via a second, more specific search and discarded that data rather than stage it here. Do not cite anything about 'Gillis Header'/CP26-52 on this row -- it belongs, if anywhere, to whatever PID tracks Cheniere's Sabine Pass-area header work, not P7807. cross_row_leads.facts: This is the ORIGINAL Gillis Access mainline (project_key 'gillis access project|tc energy' in EIA's data), distinct from the Extension row P7807. EIA's Historical Projects (1996-2024) sheet, row 1103: status Completed, in-service 2024, 42 miles, 1,500 MMcf/d, cost $400M, TC Energy. Progression across releases: Announced (2023-01) -> Construction (2024-04) -> Complete (2024-10) -> Completed (2026-05 vintage of the historical table).

TC Energy's own operations page for 'TC Louisiana Intrastate Pipeline LLC (TCLI)' states: peak capacity 1.5 Bcf/d, extends 42 miles (67.6 km), in service from 2024, originates at Gillis LA and extends to delivery points in Jefferson Davis Parish. Regulated by the Louisiana Dept. of Energy and Natural Resources' Office of Conservation (an intrastate system, not FERC-jurisdictional as of this page). Matches EIA's Completed/42-mi/1,500-MMcf/d/2024 record for the mainline.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: EIA's Aug2026 release still carries this project as 'Approved' (=GEM's proposed) with an unchanged 2027 in-service target, so the recorded proposed status is current -- not stale. The project has been continuously tracked without a gap since 2023-04 (Announced -> Approved 2024-04 -> present), so the 2-year dormancy rule does not apply; this is active, moving development, not a stalled proposal. One development worth flagging even though it does not change Status: EIA's own pipeline_type/authority fields flip this project from 'Intrastate' (through the 2026-01 release) to 'Interstate' with authority 'FERC' starting the 2026-05 release, and a docket_number field ('CP26-33, CP25-521') appears starting 2026-01 -- i.e., EIA itself now treats this as FERC-jurisdictional.
